scope: Meaning-to-IPA audit of existing heteronyms and part-of-speech-sensitive words in the three currently assembled course HTML pages. Read-only: no application or source-card changes.

coverage.method: Parsed served DATA and MT_PRONUNCIATIONS. For Mother Tongue, parsed MT_CONTEXTS, attached original excerpt/contextMeaning, and selected IPA by contextMeaning then original meaning, matching pronunciationEntry. Manually read each extracted meaning, part of speech, example and resolved IPA. Separate full-inventory multiple-IPA comparison used only as a candidate aid, not claimed as full-card semantic review.
coverage.evidence: independent-heteronym-extract.json (post-compliment-correction snapshot); findings preserve earlier faulty IPA where specified.

findings.problem: Current card is the noun meaning 칭찬 (the excerpt has brand compliments), but its stored IPA ends /mɛnt/. Merriam-Webster, Cambridge and Oxford give the noun /mənt/. Merriam-Webster gives the full /mɛnt/ ending for the verb. A deterministic audio choice from the current incorrect IPA would faithfully preserve the wrong reading.
findings.disposition: Root corrected the pronunciation source and reassembled the page on 2026-10-15. Current noun IPA is ˈkɑmpləmənt. The affected rows preserve the pre-correction evidence; generate only the corrected noun key.

findings.classification: normalization recommendation, not a confirmed error

findings.problem: The current Mother Tongue verb cards use /ˈɪmpləmənt/. Merriam-Webster and Cambridge distinguish the common American verb /ˈɪmpləˌmɛnt/ from the noun /ˈɪmpləmənt/; FABLE already uses the former for its verb card. However Collins COBUILD explicitly accepts /mənt/ as a verb variant, so calling all current cards incorrect would be too strong.
findings.disposition: Root decision: retain the current allowed variant. Keep its audio consistent with /ˈɪmpləmənt/; do not silently map it to the distinct /mɛnt/ pronunciation.

falsePositiveGuards.finding: Mother Tongue verb /ˈproʊˌtɛst/ is allowed in American English. Do not force all verb senses to second-syllable stress or label this a content error.

FABLE has first stress for reducing a price and second stress for disregarding a warning. Oxford explicitly distinguishes these senses; Cambridge presents second stress for both. Preserve supported variants rather than declaring the price verb wrong.
The two FABLE forms match the two present senses: aged ten /eɪdʒd/, aged cat /ˈeɪdʒɪd/.

Current exact read card is the present/base form /rid/, with no current /rɛd/ headword card. The UI contract reads the input headword even when an excerpt restores inflection; do not infer a required past-form clip solely from surface grammar.
Eye liquid /tɪr/ and rip /tɛr/ are correctly separated. Cambridge /ter/ uses its DRESS-vowel transcription and should not be converted into FACE /eɪ/.
Bend /baʊ/ versus weapon/knot /boʊ/ are correctly separated.

Mother Tongue 10/prev/10 has a passive refunded excerpt but primary /ˈriˌfʌnd/. This is not an error: Merriam-Webster explicitly lists both /rɪˈfʌnd/ and /ˈriˌfʌnd/ for the money-returning verb. Keep the accepted source form.

selectionRisks.risk: Existing IPA is not a pronunciation truth source by itself
selectionRisks.detail: The compliment noun shows why term + IPA lookup must be preceded by semantic validation. Keep uncertain source keys on hold instead of manufacturing authoritative-sounding clips from them.

selectionRisks.risk: Exact meaning overrides and restored excerpt forms
selectionRisks.detail: Mother Tongue resolves new contextMeaning first and originalMeaning second. The catalog extractor must use the same rule; selecting only the dictionary base or the visible inflected surface can choose a different grammatical reading.

selectionRisks.risk: IPA alternatives are display data, not two automatic utterances
selectionRisks.detail: Mixed noun/verb Mother Tongue cards retain alternatives in the displayed IPA but speak the selected primary sense. Generating every alternative as though it were independently selected would overstate coverage.

Differences in /e/ vs /ɛ/, length marks, syllable dots or optional secondary stress are not necessarily lexical heteronyms. Do not collapse primary stress, /s/ vs /z/, /ə/ vs /eɪ/, or /ɪ/ vs /aɪ/ while normalizing audio keys.

acceptedNotationDifferences.rationale: The model receives explicit stress for isolated monosyllables. The four multi-syllable aliases differ only in optional secondary-stress notation; vowel/consonant sequence and primary stress remain identical.

catalogCrosscheck.method: Directly read every compact catalog row, checked its meaning against current cards, independently converted each original IPA to the model alphabet and compared all 187 aliases. Verified r→ɹ, ɚ→əɹ, ɝ→ɜɹ, affricates ʧ/ʤ, AIOWY diphthongs and movement of stress to the next vowel. Catalog subject/object variants /ɪ/ vs /ɛ/ and implement /mənt/ vs /mɛnt/ remain separate clips.
catalogCrosscheck.limitations: This is source-semantic and phoneme-string verification. No claim is made that every generated audio waveform has been independently heard or that its naturalness is guaranteed.
